mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, observed over the last week, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility, exceeding 10 percentage points, signals improved weather or public sentiment, encouraging more outdoor and leisure activities that spill over into retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next two weeks despite PARKS rising by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in WORKPLACES mobility combined with stable RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a shift towards remote work, which reduces weekday retail activity but may increase local neighborhood retail, leading to a slight negative pressure on overall RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls > 5 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL is stable (+/- 1 point)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days, despite the specified WORKPLACES decline and stable RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of easing restrictions, a sustained increase in TRANSIT mobility over two consecutive weeks indicates growing confidence in public transport, which facilitates access to retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next 28 days, even if TRANSIT mobility rises for two consecutive weeks in an easing restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: A slight increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility while RESIDENTIAL mobility slightly decreases suggests people are venturing out more for essential services, which often precedes or coincides with increased non-essential retail activity, leading to a positive RETAIL_REC trend over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next 7 days despite GROCERY_PHARM rising and RESIDENTIAL falling week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp, sudden drop in WORKPLACES mobility, as seen in the last week, indicates a significant disruption to daily routines, likely due to new restrictions or a major event, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as fewer people commute and engage in out-of-home activities.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days following a week where WORKPLACES mobility dropped by more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in PARKS mobility, following a period of decline, suggests improving weather conditions typical for this time of year, which encourages outdoor activities and general out-of-home movement, positively influencing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility shows a week-on-week increase of more than 10 points after a prior decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, despite the observed significant rebound in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while TRANSIT mobility shows only a marginal increase, it suggests lingering public caution or continued work-from-home policies, which will suppress the full recovery of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 5% and TRANSIT increase < 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than the last 28 days, despite high RESIDENTIAL and low TRANSIT growth.
